title: Flying Domestic in NZ with Kids — Air NZ Tips, Baggage, and Seat Selection
meta_desc: Flying domestic in NZ with kids? Get Air NZ tips, baggage allowance & seat selection info to make your family trip smoother
intro: As a parent, flying domestically in NZ with kids can be a daunting task, especially when it comes to choosing the right seats and navigating baggage restrictions. With prices starting from $49 for a one-way Air NZ ticket from Auckland to Wellington, it's essential to plan ahead to ensure a stress-free journey. In this article, we'll share expert tips and insights on flying domestic with kids in NZ.

sections.heading: Air NZ Domestic Flights with Kids
sections.body: Air NZ offers a range of domestic flights that cater to families with kids. With multiple daily flights from Auckland to Queenstown, Christchurch, and Wellington, you can choose a schedule that suits your family's needs. Prices vary depending on the route and time of year, but you can expect to pay around $200-$300 for a one-way ticket from Auckland to Queenstown during peak season.

sections.heading: Family Seating Options
list: Book seats together: Air NZ allows you to book seats together for a fee of $10-$20 per person
Choose a Skycouch: Air NZ's Skycouch is a great option for families, providing a flat surface for kids to sleep or play
Opt for a bassinet: If you're traveling with an infant, consider booking a seat with a bassinet attachment

sections.heading: Queenstown vs Christchurch vs Wellington Routes
sections.body: When it comes to choosing a route, consider the drive time and activities you want to do at your destination. For example, Queenstown is a 1-hour drive from the airport, while Christchurch is a 20-minute drive. Wellington, on the other hand, has a range of family-friendly attractions, including the Te Papa Museum and Wellington Zoo.

sections.heading: Tips for Flying with Kids
list: Book a morning flight: Kids tend to be more relaxed in the morning
Pack snacks and entertainment: Bring along your kid's favorite snacks and toys to keep them occupied
Consider a portable DVD player: A portable DVD player can be a lifesaver on long flights

sections.heading: Book Your Accommodation
sections.body: Once you've booked your flights, it's time to think about accommodation. Consider booking a family-friendly hotel or apartment, such as the Novotel Queenstown Lakeside or the Quest Wellington. Prices start from around $150 per night for a family room.
